**Case 1**

The invoice that changed its bank details

*If an email asks you to pay a new account, who checks it is real?*

This is a fictional training case. On Monday 3 March a finance clerk, Priya, received an email that
looked like it came from Halden Supplies, a supplier the firm had paid for six years. The email said
Halden had moved banks and asked that the next invoice, for £48,200, be paid to a new account.

The email came from halden-supp1ies.com, with the number 1 in place of the letter l. Priya updated the
bank details in the payment system. Her manager, Tom, approved the payment run on Wednesday 5 March
without opening the change log. The money left the same afternoon.

The firm's policy said: "Any change to supplier bank details must be confirmed by phone, using a
number already on file." Nobody had made that call. The bank recovered £9,400.

When an email asks you to send money somewhere new, call the person back on a number you already
had, not one in the email.
